segments.t: Intrigued by the million-ruble prize and the chance to become head chef, Senya raises his hand with a question. Nagiyev welcomes all the kitchen cooks to participate—except for Viktor Petrovich—and explains the blind-tasting rules. Let's listen to their exchange in Russian.
Дмитрий Владимирович, а можно один вопрос?
Вдруг я выиграю и шефом стану.
Я просто заранее с тобой репетирую.
Now let's examine how Nagiyev explains the contest rules to the cooks line by line.
Дмитрий Владимирович, а можно один вопрос?
'Dmitry Vladimirovich, may I ask one question?' Senya addresses the owner politely by name and patronymic using an impersonal permission word.
'Are we allowed to participate too?' An imperfective infinitive meaning to participate pairs with a dative personal pronoun.
'Everyone is allowed, except our Vitya.' The preposition meaning except governs the genitive singular of the possessive modifier and name.
'Of course you can, my dear friends.' Nagiyev warmly encourages the rest of the kitchen staff using a vocative plural phrase.
'Thank you very much, Dima.' Senya suddenly drops all formality and addresses the restaurant owner by his first name.
Вдруг я выиграю и шефом стану.
'What if I win and become the head chef.' The perfective future verb meaning will become takes the instrumental singular on the noun for chef.
Я просто заранее с тобой репетирую.
'I am just rehearsing with you in advance.' Senya jokes that he is practicing speaking to Nagiyev as an equal before winning the job.
'I sit in a red armchair.' Nagiyev describes the show's staging using the prepositional singular of red armchair.
'I sit with my back to all the contestants.' The instrumental singular of back combines with the dative plural of participants.
'And I choose only by taste.' The preposition with the dative singular of taste expresses the criterion for judging.
'We determine the very best dish.' A first-person plural present verb takes a superlative neuter accusative noun phrase.

'Awesome, that is really original!' Fedya flatters Nagiyev's borrowed television concept using a short neuter predicate adverb. Let's hear the conversation about the contest rules again from start to finish.
Дмитрий Владимирович, а можно один вопрос?
Вдруг я выиграю и шефом стану.
Я просто заранее с тобой репетирую.

Nagiyev plans to sit in a spinning red armchair with his back to the cooks, judging dishes purely by taste. Listen for the verb meaning to participate and the nouns meaning armchair and dish. See you in the next scene.
